He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Auburn Tigers men's basketball|Auburn Tigers]]. ==Early life and high school career== Thor was born in [[Omaha, Nebraska]] to South Sudanese parents and moved to [[Anchorage, Alaska]] at age five.{{cite web |last1=Hall |first1=Erik |title=JT Thor: 5 things to know about the Auburn Tigers men's basketball forward |url=https://www.montgomeryadvertiser.com/story/sports/college/auburn/2021/01/15/jt-thor-10-facts-auburn-mens-basketball-forward-full-name/4181394001/ |website=[[Montgomery Advertiser]] |access-date=May 10, 2021 |date=January 15, 2021}} He started playing basketball in seventh grade and competed for [[West Anchorage High School]] in [[Anchorage, Alaska]].{{cite web |title=Hoops standout Thor named Alaska Athlete of the Week |url=https://alaskasportshall.org/2020/12/anchorage-hoops-standout-thor-named-alaska-athlete-of-the-week/ |website=Alaska Sports Hall of Fame |access-date=May 10, 2021 |date=December 7, 2020}} At age 14, Thor moved to West Virginia, where his brother lived, to attend [[Huntington Prep School]].{{cite web |last1=Clemente |first1=Christian |title=JT the Jokester: How JT Thor left home at 14 to pursue NBA dream |url=https://auburn.rivals.com/news/jt-the-jokester-how-jt-thor-left-home-at-14-to-pursue-nba-dream |website=[[Rivals.com|Rivals]] |access-date=May 10, 2021 |date=April 1, 2021}} After two seasons, he transferred to [[Norcross High School]] in [[Norcross, Georgia]].{{cite web |last1=Vitale |first1=Josh |title=Auburn basketball: JT Thor didn’t eat lamb, but he did show ‘next-level stuff’ vs Kentucky |url=https://www.montgomeryadvertiser.com/story/sports/college/auburn/2021/02/14/auburn-basketball-jt-thor-nba-prospect-kentucky/4430311001/ |website=[[Montgomery Advertiser]] |access-date=May 10, 2021 |date=February 13, 2021}} He reclassified to the 2020 class.{{cite web |last1=Fisher |first1=Chris |title=Five-star forward JT Thor reclassifies to 2020 |url=https://247sports.com/college/kentucky/Article/JT-Thor-reclassifies-to-2020-transfers-to-Norcross-134203144/ |website=[[247Sports.com|247Sports]] |access-date=May 10, 2021 |date=August 5, 2019}} As a senior, Thor averaged 14.9 points and 6.6 rebounds per game, receiving all-state honors.{{cite web |last1=Green |first1=Tom |title=4-star forward JT Thor officially signs with Auburn |url=https://www.al.com/auburnbasketball/2020/05/4-star-forward-jt-thor-officially-signs-with-auburn.html |website=AL.com |access-date=May 10, 2021 |date=May 11, 2020}} He was a consensus four-star recruit and committed to playing college basketball for [[Auburn Tigers men's basketball|Auburn]], choosing the Tigers over [[Oklahoma State Cowboys basketball|Oklahoma State]].{{cite web |last1=Lancaster |first1=Zach |title=JT Thor Commits to Auburn, One Spot Remaining for Boynton and Co. |url=https://www.si.com/college/oklahomastate/basketball/jt-thor-commits-auburn |website=[[Sports Illustrated]] |access-date=May 10, 2021 |date=April 12, 2020}} ==College career== On February 13, 2021, Thor recorded a freshman season-high 24 points and nine rebounds, shooting 5-of-6 from three-point range, in an 82–80 loss to [[Kentucky Wildcats men's basketball|Kentucky]].{{cite web |last1=Green |first1=Tom |title=JT Thor shows ‘next-level’ ability against Kentucky |url=https://www.al.com/auburnbasketball/2021/02/jt-thor-shows-next-level-ability-against-kentucky.html |website=AL.com |access-date=May 11, 2021 |date=February 14, 2021}} As a freshman at Auburn, he averaged 9.4 points, five rebounds and 1.4 blocks per game.{{cite web |last1=Polacheck |first1=Jacob |title=Auburn’s J.T. Thor to test NBA Draft waters |url=https://www.zagsblog.com/2021/03/23/auburns-j-t-thor-to-test-nba-draft-waters/ |website=Zagsblog |access-date=May 11, 2021 |date=March 23, 2021}} On March 23, 2021, Thor declared for the [[2021 NBA draft]] while maintaining his college eligibility.{{cite web |title=Auburn freshman JT Thor announces NBA Draft plans |url=https://www.saturdaydownsouth.com/auburn-football/jt-thor-nba-draft-2021-auburn-tigers-basketball/ |website=Saturday Down South |access-date=May 11, 2021 |date=March 23, 2021}} He later signed with an [[sports agent|agent]], forgoing his remaining eligibility.{{cite web |last=King |first=Nathan |title=JT Thor signs with agency, won't return to Auburn |url=https://247sports.com/college/auburn/Article/jt-thor-auburn-nba-draft-2021-tigers-basketball-bruce-pearl-sharife-cooper-walker-kessler-wendell-green-jr-166145584/ |website=[[247Sports.com|247Sports]] |access-date=June 6, 2021 |date=June 5, 2021}} ==Career statistics== {{NBA player statistics legend}} ===College=== {{NBA player statistics start}} |- | style="text-align:left;"| [[2020–21 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2020–21]] | style="text-align:left;"| [[2020–21 Auburn Tigers men's basketball team|Auburn]] | 27 || 27 || 23.0 || .440 || .297 || .741 || 5.0 || .9 || .8 || 1.4 || 9.4 {{S-end}} ==Personal life== Thor's older brother, Jal Rial, played basketball for [[Phoenix College]] and [[Howard College]].
